{{Short description|German physicist}}
[[File:Johannes Orphal.jpg|thumb|Orphal, Head of Division 4, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]]
'''Johannes Orphal''' (born 11 July 1966, in [[Magdeburg]]) is a German [[physicist]]. He is Head of Division 4 "Natural and Built Environment" and Full Professor of Physics at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]] (KIT). From 2009 to 2020 he was Director of the Institute of Meteorology and Climate Research (IMK) at KIT. Until 2009, he was Professor at the [[University of Paris-Est]] in [[Créteil]] and research scientist at the [[CNRS]]. 

In 2005, Orphal served as Secretary of the Organizing Committee for the Opening Ceremonies of the [[World Year of Physics 2005|World Year of Physics]] at [[UNESCO Headquarters|UNESCO headquarters]] in Paris.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wyp2005.org:80/unesco/committees.html|title=World Year of Physics 2005. Organizing Committee|date=2005-11-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051127061042/http://www.wyp2005.org:80/unesco/committees.html|access-date=2018-01-11|archive-date=2005-11-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/200502/wyp.cfm|title=World Year of Physics Opens with Paris Conference|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2018-01-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/200310/wyp.cfm|title=Here Comes the World Year of Physics|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2018-01-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/newsroom/pressreleases/wypparis.cfm|title=World Year of Physics Opens with Paris Conference|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2018-01-11|archive-date=2020-11-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101104255/https://www.aps.org/newsroom/pressreleases/wypparis.cfm|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/200502/upload/feb05.pdf|title=American Physical Society: World Year of Physics Opening Conference at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris|date=January 10, 2015|publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wyp2005.org:80/unesco/photos/index.html|title=Photos from the 2005 UNESCO WYP Opening Conference|date=2006-02-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060212053008/http://www.wyp2005.org:80/unesco/photos/index.html|access-date=2018-01-11|archive-date=2006-02-12}}</ref>  

His main scientific contributions are in the field of molecular [[spectroscopy]] applied to the Earth's [[atmosphere]]: laboratory measurements of unstable and reactive molecules and radicals, data evaluation for international databases e.g. [[HITRAN]], preparation and use of [[remote-sensing]] satellite missions ([[European Remote-Sensing Satellite|GOME]], [[SCIAMACHY]], [[MIPAS]], [[MetOp]], [[Meteosat#Third_Generation_.28.22MTG.22.29|MTG]] ...) to observe stratospheric chemistry, tropospheric air quality and processes of relevance for climate, as well as the development of sensitive in-situ measurements techniques such as [[IBBCEAS]]. 

In 2017, he was awarded the {{ill|Gentner-Kastler Prize|de|Gentner-Kastler-Preis}} of the French and German Physical Societies (SFP and DPG)<ref name="KIT">{{cite web | title=ZKU – Professor Johannes Orphal | website=KIT | url=https://www.klima-umwelt.kit.edu/640.php | language=de | access-date=13 January 2022}}</ref> and the [[Gay-Lussac Humboldt Prize]] of the [[Académie des sciences]] in Paris.<ref name="Technologie 2021">{{cite web | title=Gay-Lussac-Humboldt-Preis 2017 für Johannes Orphal | website=KIT | date=19 May 2021 | url=https://www.kit.edu/kit/pi_2018_004_gay-lussac-humboldt-preis-2017-fur-johannes-orphal.php | language=de | access-date=13 January 2022}}</ref>
